pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Welcome. Your death has been confirmed, and your memories have been preserved for evaluation.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: So… this is what happens after you die?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: In your case, yes. Before your memories can be processed, we must assess their continuity and integrity.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Your results will determine the next stage.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: What are credits supposed to mean?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Your assessment will clarify your result. Shall we begin?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: There are twenty questions. Some concern your memories, while others concern your decisions and experiences. Please answer as accurately as you can.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: And if I can't remember something?

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: People sometimes recognise places or voices without remembering where they encountered them. Has that happened to you?

choices.text: Occasionally, but I usually remember eventually.
Rarely. I trust what I remember.
Lately, more often than I'd like.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Memory recall can vary during the preservation process.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: So I might remember things later?

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Good. There are a few things I'd like to remember.

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: These images represent different types of experiences. Which would you consider most valuable to preserve?

choices.text: The clock repair. It represents a skill that could be passed on.
The embrace. Some experiences matter because of the people involved.
The diagram. Knowledge can benefit many people.
The damaged badge. Even unpleasant experiences may be worth remembering.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Are these from real people's memories?

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I feel like I've seen that before.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Familiarity has been noted. Would you like to elaborate?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: That is acceptable. We will proceed.
